Description

In the dorsal horn, μ-opioid receptors on the central terminals of nociceptors reduce glutamate release, and receptors on dorsal horn neurons hyperpolarise them through GIRK channels. Enkephalins from inhibitory interneurons and opioid drugs act at both sites through Gi/o, with Giα inhibiting adenylate cyclase. Both actions lower the transfer of nociceptive signals from the joint to the brain. Naloxone binds the same receptors without activating them and so blocks these actions.
